nodes.summary: There is a natural number $C$ such that for every $n \ge 1$ there is a finite family $\mathcal{F}$ of finite sets of natural numbers with the following properties: every member of $\mathcal{F}$ has exactly $n$ elements, any two members of $\mathcal{F}$ have a common element, every set of at most $n - 1$ natural numbers is disjoint from some member of $\mathcal{F}$, and $|\mathcal{F}| \le C n$.
nodes.title: Kahn's theorem on the Erdős–Lovász problem

nodes.summary: The statement that there is a natural number $C$ such that for every $n \ge 1$ there is a finite family $\mathcal{F}$ of finite sets of natural numbers in which every member has exactly $n$ elements, any two members have a common element, every set of at most $n - 1$ natural numbers is disjoint from some member, and $|\mathcal{F}| \le C n$. This expresses $f(n) \ll n$, where $f(n)$ is the least size of such a family.
nodes.title: Erdős Problem 21 (Erdős–Lovász)

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$, a finite family $\mathcal{F}$ of finite sets of natural numbers is an Erdős–Lovász family of order $n$ when every member of $\mathcal{F}$ has exactly $n$ elements, any two members of $\mathcal{F}$ (not necessarily distinct) have a common element, and every set of at most $n - 1$ natural numbers is disjoint from some member of $\mathcal{F}$, where $n - 1$ is read as $0$ when $n = 0$.
